newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Black Sea states vow closer ties in Moscow meeting.
newsitem.headline: Black Sea states vow closer ties in Moscow meeting.

text.p: Countries ringing the Black Sea vowed on Friday to boost trade links and to step up cooperation in energy, transport, communications and tourism, Russian news agencies reported.

In a declaration issued during a one-day meeting in Moscow, the 11 member states of the Black Sea Cooperation forum also pledged to work together to fight organised crime, terrorism and illegal trade in drugs and arms.
The forum supported peace initiatives in the Balkans and the Caucasus, where the meeting's host country Russia has agreed a truce with separatists in its breakaway Chechnya region.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said the grouping, formed in 1992 in Istanbul to promote regional ties, had evolved into an "authoritative international organisation", Interfax news agency reported.
The forum groups Russia, Turkey, Greece, Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its next half-yearly meeting will be held in Turkey.
